scope: Theorem 2.1 (Pressure law) of the manuscript “Positive scalar curvature and uniform codimension-two width” (preprints/Positive-scalar-curvature-and-uniform-codimension-two-width-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 336 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 f67c30579306bd4d), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 7. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every A0, P0, ε, b0 > 0 there exist 0 < S0 ≤ 1, T ≥ 1, and a smooth function F : (−S0, S0) × [T, ∞) −→ R which is odd in x, has Fx > 0, and satisfies Fx ≥ A0t, |Ft| ≤ ε|F|, FFt ≤ εFx, Fx ≤ b0t2 or − FFt ≥ P0Fx, Fx ≤ b0t2 + εF2 . (2.1) For each fixed t ≥ T, lim x→−S0 F(x, t) = −∞, lim x→S0 F(x, t) = +∞. These limits are uniform when t ranges over a compact subinterval of [T, ∞). The choices depend only on A0, P0, ε, b0 and fixed numerical constants. In particular, they are independent of any manifold, metric, local cutoff, or subsequent deformation parameter. The lower bound T may be increased after the construction.
